# Shared wire fixtures

Portable JSON scenarios for client implementers of Apron protocol v4. Expected
state is written from `PROTOCOL.md`, not generated by the example client or
backend. `references` holds repository-relative specification links. These
scenarios exercise selected protocol behaviors; passing them is not full
client conformance.

## Run

From the repository root, after `make install`:

```sh
make test-web   # replay fixtures and frontend unit tests
make test-wire  # session fixtures over real loopback WebSockets
make test       # both suites and Go tests; also runs in CI
```

Replay uses the frontend's existing Vitest setup. Session tests use the actual
TypeScript client with Node.js 24 WebSockets and a small Go transport peer;
no browser or running example server is needed. No new dependencies are required.

## Common structure

Each file has `format: 2`, `kind` (`replay` or `session`), `name`,
`description`, `references`, `variants`, and `expected`, and no other
top-level keys. Frames are protocol 4. Each variant has `name` and ordered
`steps`, starts with fresh client state, and must reach the top-level
`expected` state. An `expect` step additionally checks an intermediate state.

Each step is an object with exactly one key, the operation. Objects are
unordered; arrays are ordered. All IDs are JSON strings. Small IDs such as
`"100"` are readable epoch-millisecond values near the Unix epoch; they are
positive and below `2^53`, and every comparison of `log_id`s or
`message_id`s is numeric (`"9" < "10"`).

Run every variant twice: once with the literal frames, once with
`"jsonrpc": "2.0"` added at the top level of each incoming frame (including
replies built from `reply` steps). Do not alter nested data. Outgoing client
frames may use either envelope. Expectations never depend on a generated
request ID or on optional envelope fields.

## Records, replay, and the logical projection

Both suites share one client-side model (PROTOCOL.md §2, §3.4, §3.5,
Appendices A–D). The client keeps three stores, one record per key:

| record | key | sources |
|---|---|---|
| room record | `room_id` | `room` notifications (not removals), history `rooms` |
| message snapshot | `message_id` | `message` notifications, history `entries`, embedded snapshots |
| reaction set | `(message_id, user_id)` | `reactions` notifications, history `reactions` (one set per element of `reactions[]`) |

**Replay rule.** A record replaces the stored record for its key only when its
`log_id` is numerically greater; an equal or lower `log_id` is ignored. This
holds regardless of source (live, history, embedded) and arrival order. A
reaction element takes its record's `log_id`. The only exception: a room
record without `log_id` (a server without cap `history`, which may omit it)
always replaces. Replacement is whole: omitted fields disappear, objects and
arrays are never merged, and `null` is a stored value.

**Decoding.**

- Message notifications are flat snapshots:
  `{"method":"message","params":{message_id, log_id, room_id, from, body?, reply_to?, deleted?, ext?}}`.
  History `entries` are the same flat objects.
- A history result is `{rooms?, entries, reactions?, first_id?, last_id?, more, latest_log_id, history_log_id}`.
  Install every record in all three arrays. Do not filter records by the
  requested room: a move snapshot in room A's history carries `room_id` B and
  must re-home the message into B.
- `reply_to` (on messages) and `intro_message` (on room records) are message
  objects. An object with a `log_id` is an **embedded snapshot**: install it
  in the message store by the replay rule, in its own `room_id`. An object
  without `log_id` is a **bare reference** (`{message_id}`) and installs
  nothing.
- Room delivery fields (`latest_log_id`, `history_log_id`, `removed`) are not
  part of the record. A `room` frame with `removed: true` is not a record: it
  only removes the room from the visible set (sessions only).
- Unknown top-level keys (in frames, records, results, and reaction elements)
  must be ignored and may be dropped. They never break replay. Keys such as
  `"__proto__"`, `"constructor"`, `"hasOwnProperty"`, and `"toString"` appear
  as unknown keys, inside `ext`, and as room and user IDs; they must not
  pollute prototypes or collide with built-in properties.

**Message projection.** The stored snapshot restricted to the known fields
`message_id`, `log_id`, `room_id`, `from`, `body`, `reply_to`, `deleted`, and
`ext`, each present exactly when present in the snapshot and copied exactly
(`from`, `body`, and `ext` are compared deeply, including `null`s, unknown
embed kinds, and `"__proto__"` keys inside `ext`). `reply_to` is always
projected bare, as `{"message_id": ...}`. No defaults are materialized
(`body.format` stays absent when absent). Then:

- `reactions`: present only when the message is not a tombstone
  (`deleted !== true`) and at least one stored set for the message is
  non-empty. It is an array of `{"emoji": string, "user_ids": [string]}`,
  one per distinct emoji across all users' sets, sorted by emoji in Unicode
  code point order; `user_ids` are sorted by string order. Duplicate emoji in
  a set collapse. Reaction sets for messages that are not loaded are kept and
  appear once the message arrives. A tombstone hides reactions; its stored sets
  are kept but not projected.

**Room projection.** `{room_id, log_id?, parent_room_id?, title?, intro_message?, ext?, messages}`:
the optional fields come from the stored room record (absent when the record
lacks them or no record is stored), `intro_message` is projected bare as
`{"message_id": ...}`, and `messages` lists the message projections whose
current `room_id` is this room, in numeric `message_id` order. The room
projection never includes delivery fields or defaults (no `title` fallback).

Internal maps, caches, DOM elements, recovery buffers, and checkpoints are not
assertions. Compare projections exactly after the normalization above.

## Replay scenarios

A replay fixture accepts `receive` and `expect` steps and has no room of its
own; the store spans all rooms.

```json
{
  "format": 2,
  "kind": "replay",
  "name": "Creation snapshot",
  "description": "...",
  "references": ["PROTOCOL.md#35-messages"],
  "variants": [{
    "name": "live",
    "steps": [{"receive": {"method": "message", "params": {
      "message_id": "100", "log_id": "100", "room_id": "general",
      "from": {"user_id": "alice"}, "body": {"text": "original"}
    }}}]
  }],
  "expected": {"rooms": [{"room_id": "general", "messages": [
    {"message_id": "100", "log_id": "100", "room_id": "general",
     "from": {"user_id": "alice"}, "body": {"text": "original"}}
  ]}]}
}
```

`receive` holds a `message`, `room`, or `reactions` notification, or a history
response `{id, result}`. Fixed response IDs label already-issued requests;
this suite tests reduction, not request scheduling. History metadata
(`first_id`, `last_id`, `more`, `latest_log_id`, `history_log_id`) describes
the source log slice before compaction and is not interpreted by replay.

`expected` and `expect` are `{"rooms": [...]}`: every room that has a stored
record or at least one message currently homed in it, sorted by `room_id` in
string order, each in the room projection above.

| file | covers |
|---|---|
| `01-creation.json` | flat creation snapshot, live and from history |
| `02-full-replacement.json` | omitted `body.format`, `reply_to`, and `ext` namespaces are removed; `ext` replaced, not merged |
| `03-literal-null.json` | `null` stored inside `ext` and embeds |
| `04-array-replacement.json` | embeds arrays replaced whole |
| `05-tombstone.json` | tombstone wins over stale content; tombstones hide reactions (raw and compacted history) |
| `06-duplicate-replay.json` | repeated room records, snapshots, and reaction sets are ignored |
| `07-snapshot-loaded.json` | history snapshot replaces a loaded message |
| `08-snapshot-unloaded.json` | an edit installs without its creation |
| `09-history-equivalence.json` | live, raw page, two pages delivered newest-first, and compacted page converge across all record kinds |
| `10-ext-and-unknown-keys.json` | `ext` survives exactly; unknown and prototype-like keys, room IDs, and user IDs are safe |
| `11-numeric-ordering.json` | numeric `log_id` comparison for every kind; numeric `message_id` order |
| `12-room-moves.json` | move into a thread room re-homes rather than deletes; move snapshot in both rooms' history; stale source pages cannot pull it back; reactions follow |
| `13-room-records.json` | room records replace in full; embedded `intro_message`; stale room record; thread room with `parent_room_id` |
| `14-reactions.json` | per-user sets, duplicate collapse, `[]` clears, reactions before their message, folded compacted records |
| `15-embedded-snapshots.json` | `reply_to` and `intro_message` snapshots install by the replay rule; stale embeds ignored; bare and dangling references install nothing |

The TypeScript adapter is
[`clients/web/src/lib/protocol/wire-replay.test.ts`](../../../clients/web/src/lib/protocol/wire-replay.test.ts).
Another client needs only a JSON loader, a frame-to-store adapter, and the
projection above.

## Session scenarios

Session fixtures use `kind: "session"`. They drive the real client over a
transport: the fixture plays the server, and operation steps call the
client's public API.

### Steps

| step | meaning |
|---|---|
| `receive: frame` | Deliver the literal server frame. |
| `request: {as, match}` | Take the next matching outgoing client request (see below), assert it, and capture its runtime `id` under `as`. |
| `reply: {to, result}` / `reply: {to, error}` | Send `{id, result}` or `{id, error}` for the request captured as `to`. |
| `send: {as, room, text, format, reply_to?}` | Post a message to `room`; `reply_to` is a message ID. |
| `editMessage: {as, message_id, text}` | Save the message with only `body.text` changed. |
| `moveMessage: {as, message_id, room}` | Save the message with `room_id` changed to `room`. |
| `deleteMessage: {as, message_id}` | Save the message as a tombstone. |
| `react: {as, message_id, emojis}` | Set the user's complete emoji set on the message (`[]` clears). |
| `createRoom: {as, parent_room_id?, title?, intro_message_id?}` | Create a room; with `parent_room_id` it is a thread. |
| `updateRoom: {as, room, title?, intro_message_id?}` | Patch a room's metadata: a present key sets the value (`null` clears it), an absent key keeps the current value. |
| `loadRoom: {as, room}` | Open a thread room (a room with `parent_room_id`): load its history as its own room. |
| `disconnect: true` | Close the transport; subsequent frames go to a fresh connection. |
| `expect: state` | Wait for the given keys of the session state (bounded deadline). |

Each operation step (`send` through `loadRoom`) tracks its outcome under its
`as` label in `operations`: `pending` when invoked, then `fulfilled` or
`rejected`. Mutations settle on the reply to their request: a `result`
fulfills, an `error` rejects. They never wait for a broadcast; the broadcast
may arrive before or after the result. `loadRoom` fulfills when its last page
(`more: false`) is applied and rejects on an error or invalid page. Operation and capture labels are unique
within a variant.

### Request matching

A `request` step selects the oldest queued client request whose `method`
equals `match.method` and whose `params.room_id` and `params.message_id` each
equal the value in `match.params`, where absent equals absent. Unrelated
requests (for example `me` or `activity`) may be pipelined or reordered and
stay queued. Then:

- `match` is a recursive subset of the frame: objects match by listed keys;
  arrays and scalars match exactly. Extra fields such as `auth.params.name`,
  `auth.params.client`, and `history.params.limit` are unconstrained.
- For mutations (`message`, `room`, `reactions`) `params` must equal
  `match.params` exactly, to catch lost or unwanted fields.
- Captured IDs must be strings, distinct from every earlier captured ID in the
  variant.

### What a conforming client sends

These are exact (PROTOCOL.md §3.5, Appendices B–D). "Latest snapshot" and
"latest record" mean the stored record under the replay rule at the moment the
operation is invoked.

| operation | method | `params` |
|---|---|---|
| `send` | `message` | `{room_id: room, body: {text, format}, reply_to?: {message_id}}` |
| `editMessage` | `message` | latest snapshot's client fields with `body.text` replaced: `{message_id, room_id, body, reply_to?, ext?}`; `body` keeps `format`, `embeds`, and any other body keys |
| `moveMessage` | `message` | `{message_id, room_id: room, body, reply_to?, ext?}` from the latest snapshot |
| `deleteMessage` | `message` | `{message_id, room_id, reply_to?, ext?, deleted: true}` from the latest snapshot; no `body` |
| `react` | `reactions` | `{message_id, emojis}` with `emojis` as given |
| `createRoom` | `room` | `{parent_room_id?, title?, intro_message?: {message_id}}`: only the keys given; no `room_id`, no `ext` |
| `updateRoom` | `room` | `{room_id, title?, intro_message?: {message_id}, ext?}` from the latest record with the patch applied; never `parent_room_id` |
| (recovery) | `history` | `{room_id, after, before}` plus an optional positive `limit` |
| (connect) | `auth` | `{scheme: "guest"}` plus optional `name`/`client` |

In saves, `reply_to` is always resubmitted bare even when the stored snapshot
embedded it, `ext` is resubmitted unchanged (including `"__proto__"` keys),
`deleted` is omitted unless deleting, and fields absent from the latest
snapshot stay absent. Room updates resubmit `intro_message` bare and `ext`
unchanged.

### History recovery profile

The fixtures pin the example client's recovery profile. It is a test profile
built from PROTOCOL.md Appendix A, not
the only conforming strategy. The recovery state below is kept per room across
a lost connection (see Session state); a room announced for the first time
starts without it.

- **Head and bound.** Per visible room the client tracks its known head, the
  greatest `latest_log_id` from that room's `room` frames and history results
  and `log_id` of live records delivered with that `room_id`, and its floor F,
  the greatest effective lower bound seen: `history_log_id`, or the same
  frame's or page's own `latest_log_id + 1` when it is `null`. Before any
  bound is seen there is no F.
- **Eviction.** When F grows, the client drops the room's messages whose stored
  snapshot `log_id` is below F, drops buffered and newly received message and
  reaction records below F, and ignores page records below F. Room records are
  not evicted.
- **Automatic recovery** (cap `history`, rooms without `parent_room_id`, no
  recovery already running), with H = the known head:
  - A `room` frame starts one when the room is announced with no kept state,
    when its last recovery failed, when there is no checkpoint C yet, or when
    the known head is above C. It is a **rebuild** (clear the room's messages
    and their reaction sets, start at `after = F`) for a room with no kept
    state, after a failure, or with no C; otherwise it **resumes** at
    `after = max(C + 1, F)` and keeps the room's state. A room kept from a
    lost connection whose head has not moved past C needs no request.
  - When F grows outside a recovery and there is no C or `C + 1 < F`, a rebuild
    starts.
  - If `after > H` the recovery completes with no request.
- **Pages.** Request `{room_id, after, before: H}`, apply each valid page's
  records, and continue from `last_id + 1` (numerically) while `more`. H never
  changes during a recovery, even when frames or pages report a newer head.
- **Live records during recovery** for that room are buffered and applied when
  the recovery completes or fails. A `room` frame during a recovery never
  starts another one.
- **Overtaken.** If a page's bound, or F after a `room` frame, is greater than
  the pending `after`, history was discarded: ignore that page and any pending
  request, rebuild from the new F with the same H, and keep buffered records at
  or above F. A bound equal to `after` only evicts.
- **Completion.** Apply the buffer; C becomes `max(C, H)`.
- **Failure.** An `error` reply; a result lacking an `entries` array, a
  boolean `more`, a valid `latest_log_id`, or a `history_log_id` that is null
  or a valid ID; or a `more: true` page whose `last_id` is below `after` or not
  below H. The client applies the pages it has and the buffer, leaves C
  unchanged, and marks the room failed; the next `room` frame for it rebuilds.
  A failure is not retried on a timer (the `retry_after` variant's
  `data.retry_after` is not waited on).
- **Thread rooms** never recover automatically. `loadRoom` loads one with
  H = its known head when invoked, `after` = F, or
  `max(T + 1, F)` given the thread's own checkpoint T from an earlier
  `loadRoom`, kept across a lost connection. Pages apply as they arrive; if F overtakes
  `after`, continue from F. T advances to each page's `last_id` and to H at
  `more: false`. Live records for the thread apply directly.

The fixtures assert no state while a recovery has requests in flight; they
assert after completion, after failure, or before recovery starts.

### Session state

The normalized session state has these keys:

- `you`: the identity from the latest successful `auth` result on the current
  connection, or `null`.
- `caps`: the latest `server` frame's `caps` sorted by string order; `[]` when
  omitted or before any `server` frame on the connection.
- `rooms`: the visible rooms (announced on the current connection and not
  since removed) sorted by `room_id` in string order, each in the room
  projection above. Only server records appear; optimistic local echoes do
  not.
- `typing`: active typing indicators `{room_id, from}` (Appendix D.1),
  sorted by `room_id` then `from.user_id`. An `activity` frame with
  `typing > 0` adds or refreshes one; `typing: 0` removes it; an `activity`
  frame without `typing` leaves it unchanged. Fixture servers that send
  `activity` advertise cap `activity`.
- `operations`: operation labels mapped to `pending`, `fulfilled`, or
  `rejected`.

On `disconnect` the client's protocol view is rebuilt from the next
connection: `you` is `null`, `caps` and `typing` are `[]`, and `rooms` is `[]`
until rooms are announced again. The record stores, floors, and checkpoints
are kept, so each re-announced room resumes from its checkpoint rather than
recovering in full (PROTOCOL.md Appendix A, recovery from `C + 1`). (The UI may keep showing the old view meanwhile; that is not part
of the projection.) A pending operation across a disconnect is unconstrained.

An omitted top-level `expected` key is unconstrained; `expected: {}` means
each variant ends with its own `expect`. Supplied values compare exactly.
Adapters wait for state changes with bounded deadlines; fixture files contain
no sleeps, timers, or DOM selectors.

| file | covers |
|---|---|
| `core-session.json` | guest auth, `activity` typing, sends in both confirmation orders, bare `reply_to` answered by an embedded snapshot, `server` replacement, unknown notifications, room records without `log_id` |
| `message-saves.json` | edit, move into a thread room, and delete resubmit `room_id`, `body`, bare `reply_to`, and `ext` from the latest snapshot |
| `rooms.json` | thread and top-level creation, patch-style updates resubmitting `title`, `intro_message`, and `ext`, full record replacement, removal |
| `reactions.json` | react, change, clear, move re-log in the destination, `invalid_params`, tombstone hiding |
| `request-errors.json` | denied send, save, and room creation keep the session usable |
| `history-live-boundary.json` | fixed H with live records above it (edit, room update, reaction), mixed-kind pages (limit counts every kind), raw and compacted |
| `history-boundaries.json` | inclusive bound with eviction, bound overtaking a recovery by `room` frame or by page, sparse IDs, `null` bounds (empty log, expired cache, becoming retained, page head) |
| `history-recovery-failure.json` | a head above the checkpoint resumes from `C + 1`; an error or invalid page keeps partial and buffered state; the next `room` frame rebuilds |
| `reconnect-history.json` | new guest identity after reconnect; recovery resumes from the kept checkpoint, across message and reaction records |
| `thread-recovery.json` | thread room recovered only by `loadRoom`, as its own room; move in both rooms' logs; interleaved with room recovery |

The Node adapter is [`tests/interop/wire.spec.ts`](../../interop/wire.spec.ts).
Its [`wire-peer.go`](../../interop/wire-peer.go) utility only transports frames;
it contains no chat behavior or expected state. Each test gets a fresh client
connection. Alternative implementations can use any transport harness that
preserves these exchanges and projections.

## Fixture invariants

Every session variant describes one plausible server, and these hold (they
were checked with an independent reference reducer and client):

- Each `log_id` names one record (one key, one content) across the whole
  variant, across connections, and in embedded copies. `log_id`s are one
  server-wide sequence: new live records on a connection arrive in strictly
  increasing order, and above every `latest_log_id` already reported for their
  room. A message's earliest snapshot is its creation, with
  `log_id == message_id`.
- A `room` frame's `latest_log_id` is at least every record already delivered
  for the room; a page's is at least the room's head known when it was
  requested and at least its `last_id` (it may be captured before later live
  frames). A non-null `history_log_id` never exceeds `latest_log_id`, and the
  effective bound never decreases. Records may be missing from live delivery
  (a server may drop notifications); a later head reveals them.
- A room's log holds its room records, its reaction records, and every
  snapshot of a message that was in the room just before or after it, so a
  move appears in both rooms.
- History pages hold only records of the requested room within
  `[after, before]`, ascending per array. `first_id`/`last_id` span the slice
  before compaction; records missing inside it were compacted into later
  records of the same key in the page. The slice starts at the first record at
  or after `after`, and `more` is true exactly when records remain up to
  `before`. The server clamps `limit` per file (stated in each description)
  and counts records of every kind.
- Mutation results name the saved message, the created message's creation
  snapshot, or the created or updated room; `reactions` results are `{}`.

Replay variants obey the same one-record-per-`log_id` rule and the history
metadata constraints that do not depend on request bounds.

## Scope and additions

Keep fixture expectations explicit and reviewable. Add variants only when
they must produce the same final state (or use `expected: {}` with a final
`expect` per variant); use intermediate `expect` steps when ordering matters.
Keep the invariants above when adding frames. Use generated data for volume
benchmarks rather than large checked-in logs.

Not covered: `room_join`/`room_leave`, `me` response semantics, typing
expiry, read markers, deduplication lifetime, embeds and uploads, push, RTC, WebAuthn (see
`tests/fixtures/webauthn.json`), renderer behavior, and performance.
